Gyulahaza Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Gyulaháza, Hungary

Not demolished. Believed founded in the late 18th century, though its oldest surviving tombstone dates only to 1862, this cemetery remained in use until at least 1944. The first four Jews settled in Gyulaháza around 1747; the community grew to a peak of 168 by 1880 before declining to 61 by 1941. It maintained a small synagogue and religious school with an employed shochet, but ceased to be an independent community in 1895, joining Kisvárda's larger Jewish institutions. Two Jewish soldiers from Gyulaháza died in World War I, and antisemitic laws later triggered a small pogrom in which Jewish shop windows were smashed. In 1944, the entire community was deported via the Kisvárda Ghetto to Auschwitz; 15 survivors returned, mostly from forced labor camps, but the community was never re-established.
